extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scientific investigators, and students of Baconian method / philosophy of science
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting Baconian induction: collect a suffcient natural and experimental history, arrange observations into tables, and derive 'forms' (causes/laws) by systematic comparison (agreement, difference, degrees) and backward inference from ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect a sufficient natural and experimental history
rubrics_metrics.description: Primo enim paranda est historia naturalis et experimentalis, sufficiens et bona; quod fundamentum rei est : neque enim fino-endum, aut excogitandum, sed inveniendum, quid natura faciat aut ferat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The history (collection of observations and experiments) is the foundation and must be discovered, not invented. It should be 'sufficing and good' — extensive, varied, and factual. Avoid assembling data in a way that confuses the intellect; collect according to what nature actually presents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange observations into tables (ministratio ad memoriam)
rubrics_metrics.description: Historia naturalis et experimentalis tam varia est et sparsa, ut intellectum confundat et disgreget, nisi sistatur et compareat ordine idoneo. Itaque formandae sunt tabulae et coordinationes instantiarum, tali modo et instructione ut in eas agere possit intellectus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create organized tables of instances so the intellect can act upon them. The 'ministratio ad memoriam' organizes raw observations into usable forms. The tables should enable comparison and avoid leaving data 'scattered'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use three ministrations: sense, memory (tables), and mind (induction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior autem trifariam dividitur : in tres nempe ministrationes ; ministrationem ad sensum, ministrationem ad memoriam, et ministrationem ad mentem sive rationem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Ministratio ad sensum: collect observations/experiments. 2) Ministratio ad memoriam: arrange them in tables. 3) Ministratio ad mentem/sive rationem: perform induction (draw inferences). Each stage is necessary; intellect alone is incompetent without the other two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induction must be legitimate and regulated (indictio legitima)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhibenda est indictio legitima et vera, quae ipsa clavis est interpretationis. Incipiendum autem est a fine, et retro pergendum ad reliqua.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inductive inference must be guided by a true key/indication — a regulated method. Begin from the end (desired explanation) and proceed backward through the data. Do not allow unregulated intuition; the intellect must be armed and governed by proper indicia and experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin from the end and work backward
rubrics_metrics.description: Incipiendum autem est a fine, et retro pergendum ad reliqua.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with the targeted phenomenon or final condition and reconstruct the causal chain backward (retrograde approach). This backward procedure helps derive causes (forms) from effects and sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make comparative tables: Agreement, Privation (Difference), and Degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Instantiae convenientes in natura calidi ... (Table of instances where phenomenon is present); Instantiae in proximo, quae privantur natura calidi (instances where it is absent); Tabula graduum, sive comparativae in calido (comparative/degrees table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Table of Agreement (instances sharing the phenomenon), the Table of Difference/Privation (similar cases where phenomenon is lacking), and the Table of Degrees (cases showing increase/decrease). Apply these to isolate the cause via Methods of Agreement, Difference, and Degree (examples and explanation given in notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect 'instances convenientes' according to actual occurrence order
rubrics_metrics.description: Historia vero naturalis et experimentalis tam varia est et sparsa, ut intellectum confundat ... Id quoque licet fiat, tamen intellectus sibi permissus, et sponte movens, incompetens est ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather instances as they present themselves in nature (not in a preconceived order). The proper order for analysis is chosen after collection to avoid overlooking materially relevant instances. Avoid preselecting only convenient examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare across dissimilar materials to find common natures
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquisitio formarum sic procedit ; super naturam datam primo facienda est comparentia ad intellectum omnium instantiarum notarum, quae in eadem natura conveniunt, per materias licet dissimillimas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To identify the 'form' of a phenomenon, compare instances across heterogeneous materials that nevertheless exhibit the phenomenon, so common circumstances can be identified. This comparison isolates what is essential and independent of particular substrate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate and resolve composite bodies by reasoned induction, not by destructive fire
rubrics_metrics.description: Itaque facienda est corporum separatio et solutio : non per ignem certe, sed per rationem et inductionem veram, cum experimentis auxiliaribus ; et per comparationem ad alia corpora, et reductionem ad naturas simplices et earum formas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on crude destructive methods (e.g., fire) that create misleading alterations; instead use rational separation, auxiliary experiments, comparisons, and reduction to simple natures and their 'forms'. The goal is true analysis of composite structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate latent processes and their temporal/continuous sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Latens autem Processus ... plane processum continuatum, qui maxima ex parte sensum fugit. ... Exempli gratia ... in omni generatione et transformatione corporum, inquirendum quid deperdatur et evolet, quid maneat, quid accedat ; quid dilatetur, quid contrahatur ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the hidden (latent) processes that operate through time and often escape direct sensation. Map sequences: what precedes, what follows, what increases/decreases, what unites/separates — these chronologies are essential to understand causes and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate latent schematism (ultimate constitution/configuration) of bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Similiter, inquisitio et inventio latentis schematismi in corporibus res nova est ... Nam by the 'Latent schematism' Bacon seems to mean the configuration and relative position of the ultimate particles of bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probe internal structure, arrangement of ultimate particles, textures, pores, fibers, and other micro-constitutions. This anatomy of homogeneous matter is difficult but necessary to discover specific properties and the norms of alteration/transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish inquiry into 'forms' (laws/essences) from inquiry into concrete serial processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Praeceptum sive axioma de transformatione corporum duplicis est generis ... Primum intuetur corpus, ut sive conjugationem naturarum simplicium ... At secundum genus axiomatis (quod a latentis processu inventione pendet) non per naturas simplices procedit, sed per concreta corpora ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize two kinds of transformation inquiries: (1) by assembling simple natures (superinducing attributes) and (2) by discovering the latent natural process in concrete successive stages. Both have different uses: the first suits primary action (operativa), the second is nearer-at-hand and promising in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary axioms about simple natures underpin radical operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pars contemplativa ... ad primaria illa et catholica axioma de naturis simplicibus ... Sed altiores et radicales operationes super naturam pendent utique ab axiomatibus primariis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental general axioms about simple natures (forms/laws) provide the basis for higher, radical operations (capable of transforming nature). Seek these primary axioms since they enable profound practical interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate multiplicity into simplicity and the vague into the definite (mathematize where appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quo magis vergit inquisitio ad naturas simplices, eo magis omnia erunt sita in plano et perspicuo ; translato negotio a multiplici in simplex, et ab incommensurabili ad commensurabile, et ab surdo ad computable, et ab infinito et vago ad definitum et certum ; ut fit in elementis literarum, et tonis concentuum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce complex, immeasurable phenomena into simple, measurable, definite elements. Apply mathematical treatment where suitable (e.g., enumeration, mensuration) to make problems tractable and precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid letting unregulated intellect draw conclusions; restrain by method and experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Id quoque licet fiat, tamen intellectus sibi permissus, et sponte movens, incompetens est et inhabillis ad opificium axiomatum, nisi regatur et muniatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unaided reasoning is unreliable for producing axioms. The intellect must be governed and supplied with properly organized data, tables, legitimate indications, and auxiliary experiments before attempting induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use auxiliary experiments and comparisons to test and refine inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Itaque facienda est corporum separatio et solutio ... cum experimentis auxiliaribus ; et per comparationem ad alia corpora, et reductionem ad naturas simplices et earum formas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform designed auxiliary experiments and comparative tests to confirm or refute candidate causes/forms. Use reduction and comparative analysis as active validation steps rather than mere speculation.
